newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Shrinking S.Korean trade deficit headed right way.
newsitem.headline: Shrinking S.Korean trade deficit headed right way.

text.p: A sharp narrowing in South Korea's trade deficit in May from a year ago was welcomed by economists and analysts, who said on Monday they were optimistic the improvement would continue.
The trade ministry said the nation's customs-cleared trade deficit shrank dramatically to $686 million in May from a $1.44 billion shortfall a year earlier.
"The narrowing trade deficit confirms our view that the trade deficit will improve in the second-half," said Namuh Rhee, head of research at Dongbang Peregrine Securities.
The customs-cleared trade deficit totalled $9.56 billion in the first five months of this year, up from $7.65 billion in the same period of 1996.
"It is encouraging to see things are going in a more positive direction. Of course, $686 million is not in itself a tiny deficit," said Henry Morris, managing director at Coryo International Ltd.
"There's a long road ahead before Korea can return to a positive trade balance, but the trend is certainly very encouraging."
The ministry said FOB exports rose 3.9 percent in May year-on-year, while CIF imports fell 2.5 percent.
The May increase in exports marked the second straight monthly rise for 1997. Exports declined in the January to March period.

"We have expected this direction in the trade account. Exports have continued to recover starting at the end of last year, especially in volume terms," said Tae Chung, strategist for Jardine Fleming Securities.
"What we still are concerned about is the sustainability of the price recovery of key exports."
Semiconductor exports gained 8.8 percent in May, the first year-on-year rise in 13 months, the ministry said.
"It appears the semiconductor export problem, which has been the major factor behind the ballooning trade deficit, has eased to some extent," it said.
On the other hand, exports excluding semiconductors rose 3.2 percent. That rate of growth was far slower than the 9.6 percent rise in April, the ministry said.
"A rise in export growth has continued in heavy industrial and chemical products sectors such as automobiles, steel products and petrochemical goods," the ministry said.
"But the growth in light industrial exports such as shoes, textile products, toys, dolls, plastic goods, leather and fur products, has slowed," it said.
The ministry said May's decline in imports was the first such drop in the past eight months.
The ministry said slowing crude imports and a slowdown in capital and consumer goods purchases were responsible for the overall decline in imports.
"The deficit in May proves that the imports have started to reflect the nation's depressed economy," said Hwang In-seong, senior economist at Samsung Economic Research Institute.

"The trade deficit is forecast to improve in the remaining months of this year largely on the back of falling imports and also on exports increase." Chung at Jardine Fleming agreed, but said he does not see the speed of improvement accelerating.
"Even if the Korean economy has hit the bottom, the bottoming out process will be slow until we (have) seen an improvement in the export environment and that is not likely in the foreseeable future."
